strings.name: Caeleb Dressel
strings.summary: Caeleb Dressel became a U.S. sprint leader through freestyle, butterfly, fast starts and underwater technique. He won nine Olympic golds across Rio, Tokyo and Paris and multiple long-course world titles. After a 2022 break, he discussed mental health and rediscovering enjoyment, returned gradually and qualified for international short-course competition in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Multiple Olympic and world titles give him international competitive influence in sprint swimming.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Green Cove Springs, Florida, United States
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Attended the University of Florida; collegiate team, 2014–2018
strings.highlights.h1.title: Nine Olympic golds
strings.highlights.h1.text: Two in Rio, five in Tokyo and two in Paris, including preliminary relay contributions.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Long-course world success
strings.highlights.h2.text: Seven golds in 2017; six golds and two silvers in 2019.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Short-course trials return
strings.timeline.t1.text: Won the 50m freestyle and 100m individual medley and qualified for short-course worlds.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Two Paris relay golds
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won men’s 4× 100m freestyle and mixed 4× 100m medley gold, swimming preliminaries in the latter.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Worlds withdrawal and break
strings.timeline.t3.text: Left mid-meet, took an extended break and returned to competition in 2023.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Five Tokyo golds
strings.timeline.t4.text: Won three individual and two relay titles.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Gwangju worlds
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won six golds and two silvers and broke the then 100m butterfly world record.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Budapest worlds
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won seven gold medals across individual and relay events.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First Olympics in Rio
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won two relay golds with the United States.
strings.timeline.t8.title: College swimming begins
strings.timeline.t8.text: Joined Florida’s program and developed his sprint specialties.
